BRIEF FACTS:
2. Brief facts of the case are that on 08.07.2019, Sh.
Naresh Kumar Sharma, the Food Safety Officer took a sample of "Paneer" for analysis under the provisions of FSS Act/Rules/ Regulations from Food Business OperatorcumPartner Sh. Aakash Bhutani from the premises of M/s Leo's Restaurant & Bar (A Unit of UR Foods), 164345, GF, Main Bazar, Pahar Ganj, Delhi, where the said food article was stored ready for use in the preparation of Paneer Tikka, Achari Paneer Tikka, Haryali Paneer Tikka, Paneer Tikka Roll, Chili Paneer, Shahi Paneer, Cream Paneer and other Paneer Vegetables/Subji for human consumption.

After disclosing his identity to the FBOcum Partner Sh. Aakash Bhutani, FSO showed his intention of taking a sample of 'Paneer' for analysis and tried to associate some public witnesses by requesting passerby visitors and customers but none came forward.
Smt. Suvidha, FSO was present there and agreed to join the sample proceedings as witness.
The sample consisted of approx. 1 Kg. of "Paneer" (ready for use) was taken after cutting into smallest possible size with the help of a clean & dry knife in a clean & dry steel tray.

The sample was transferred equally into four clean & dry glass bottles with the help of same spoon and 20 drops of formalin were added to each sample counterpart with the help of a clean & dry dropper.
Each bottle containing the sample was separately marked, packed, fastened and sealed according to the provisions of FSS Act/Rules/Regulations.
The FBO's signature were obtained on the Designated Officer slip bearing signature of the Designated Officer and wrapper of the bottle containing the sample.
The signatures of Sh. Aakash Bhutani, FBOcumPartner were obtained on the labels of all the four counterparts of the sample.
3. Notice in Form VA was prepared on the spot and the same was given to Sh. Aakash Bhutani.
Price of Rs.200/ was paid to Sh. Aakash Bhutani as a cost of approx. 1 kg "Paneer".
Panchnama was prepared on the spot and all the documents prepared during sampling were read over and explained to FBO cumPartner, who signed the same after understanding it.

On 09.07.2019, one part of the sample bearing sample code number 129/1054/46/2019 and the Designated Officer Code number 01/DO24/14124 in intact condition along with copy of Memo in FormVI in a sealed packet along with another copy of memo in Form VI under sealed cover were sent separately to the Food Analyst,
Delhi.
The other two counterparts of the sample along with two copies of Memorandum in Form VI were deposited with the then Designated Officer, District Central.

FBO did not request to send the fourth counterpart of the sample for analysis by NABL Accredited Laboratory under Rule 2.4.5 of FSS Rules and the same was deposited with the Designated Officer, District Central in intact condition in a sealed packed on 09.07.2019.

4. The copy of the Food Analyst was sent to the FBO cumPartner giving him an opportunity to file an appeal against the report and for sending one part of the sample to the Referral Food Laboratory,
if he so desires.
But none appeared before the Designated Officer to file an appeal.

sentences.text: 5. M/s UR Foods (Owner of Unit Leo's Restaurant & Bar), is a partnership concern having three partners namely Sh. Aakash Bhutani, Sh. Simerdeep Singh Sahni and Sh. Mani Sahni.
All these partners looked after daytoday conduct of its business and they are incharge and responsible for the conduct and its business and liable for the offence.
The FBO firm being a partnership firm M/s UR Foods (Owner of Unit Leo's Restaurant & Bar), is also liable for the offence.
After conclusion of the investigation, the case file along with the statutory documents and report of Food Analyst were sent to the Designated Officer, District Central.

Sh. Hukum Singh, Department of Food Safety, has accorded sanction under Section 36(3)(e) of FSS Act and directed the undersigned to file an application before the concerned Adjudicating Officer/Addl. District Magistrate (District Central)
for the purpose of adjudication of the offence.
6. The Adjudicating Officer (in short "AO") give show cause notice to the appellants and they filed their reply on 03.03.2021 before him.
The appellants also filed written arguments.
Thereafter, vide impugned order, appellants were held guilty for selling substandard paneer and were imposed the penalties as mentioned in Para no. 1 of this order.

GROUNDS OF APPEAL:
7.
The impugned order is assailed inter alia on the grounds that the Ld. AO has erred in not taking into consideration the written submission/reply filed by them.
The FSO has not mentioned in his complaint as to what was the strength and expiry date of the formalin.
As per the report of the Food Analyst, the sample contains added vegetable oil but no percentage of vegetable oil was given by Food Analyst.
As per the standard of Paneer Regulation no. 2.1.1.6 of the FSS (FPS & FA), it nowhere mention the parameter of Butyrorefractometer in the standard of Paneer.
Only two parameters are given in standard of Paneer (i) Moisture Maximum and (ii) Milk Fat dry matter basis.

The Food Analyst is required to mention that seal was compared on the container and the outer cover with specimen impression of seal received separately,
but nowhere it is so mentioned by the Food Analyst.
The Food Analyst has not mentioned in his report that as to which test method was applied for analysis of the sample commodity.
The same is required to be given in the report.
The Ld. AO failed to consider that the sampled commodity was not for direct sale.

The penalty imposed by the Ld. AO is excessive and was imposed on all appellants and they deserve lenient view.
8.
The respondent has not filed any reply against this appeal.
9. Heard arguments of Sh. Nirjhar Pandey and Ms. Saloni, Ld. Counsel for the appellants and Sh. Vinod Kumar Sharma, Ld. Chief PP for the State/respondent.
Perused the record of the Adjudicating Officer and the present appeal and documents filed therewith.

There is also no evidence on record to show that so called extracted oil from the food stuff was sufficient for the purpose of analysis.

sentences.text: In this case, the sample of haldi and rice were tken by the Food Inspector from the jail premises and the same were not found in conformity with the prescribed standard and were held to be adulterated.

In background of this case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court observed that the food items which were found to be adulterated were not stored for sale but for meant for consumption of the inmates and storage of an adulterated article of food other than for sale does not come within the mischief of Section 16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
Thereby the facts of the present case are distinguishable from the facts of this case.

14. The other contention raised on behalf of appellant is that there is no mention in the report of Public Analyst of the method adopted to analyse the sample and accordingly, the report of the Analyst loose its credibility.

In State of Gujarat v Safimohmmad Rasulbhai Nakum (Supra), the Hon'ble Gujarat High Court observed that there is no mention in the report of the Public Analyst of any method by which the samples were found to be adulterated.

In support of his submission, he has relied upon Dhian Singh v Municipal Board (Supra).

Here the court has endorsed the view taken by the Hon'ble Allahabad High Court in Nagar Mahapalika of Kanpur v Sri Ram (1963) All. LJ 765 observing that report of Public Analyst under Section 13 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, need not contain the mode or particulars of analysis nor the test applied but should contain the result of analysis namely, data from which it can be inferred whether the article of food was or was not adulterated as defined in Section 2(1) of the Act.

sentences.text: 15. In view of the law laid down by the Apex Court, the submission made by the appellants that non mentioning of the test method applied in the present case for analysis of sample commodity render the report of the Food Analyst unreliable, is not acceptable.

16. The other contention raised on behalf of Ld. Counsel for the appellants is that FSO has not mentioned in his complaint as to what was the strength and expiry date of Formalin, there is no positive evidence that the bottle in which sample was collected was dry and clean at the spot and there is no evidence to show that so called extracted oil from the food stuff was sufficient for the purpose of analysis.
It is relevant to mention here that perusal of the Food Analyst report reveals that seals were intact & identical to the specimen impression of the seal received from Food Officer.

Further, perusal of Form VA prepared at the spot by the FSO reveal that approx. 1 kg "Paneer" was taken as sample from an tray after cutting into smallest possible size with the help of a clean and dry steel knife in a clean & dry steel tray.

The sample was mixed properly with the help of a clean & dry steel spoon in the same tray by rotating in all possible directions and then transferred the sample equally into four clean & dry glass bottles with the help of same spoon.
20 drops of formalin added into each sample counterpart with the help of a clean & dry dropper.

17. Perusal of the record available with this court reveal that strength and expiry date of formalin is not mentioned anywhere but, what is the relevancy of the same has not been elaborated by the appellants.
Moreover, an option was given to the appellant to get the sample tested from any other NABL Accredited Lab but this option was not availed.
Thereby, in view of this court not mentioning of strength and expiry date of formalin has not caused any prejudice to the appellants and same deserves to be ignored.
Further, on the basis of Form VA, it is apparent that all fair procedure was adopted by the FSO to take the sample and same was put in the clean & dry glass bottles.
This court finds no reason to disbelieve this report of FSO prepared on Form VA i.e. Form of Notice to the Food Business Operator.

18. Another important contention raised on behalf of appellants is that as per FSS (FP&A)
Regulations, it is nowhere mentioned about the parameters of Butyro Refractometer in the sample of Paneer.
Regulation 2.1.16 of FSS (FP&A) Regulations prescribes standards for Chhana and Paneer.
For better appreciation of the facts, Regulation 2.1.16 of FSS (FP&A) Regulations, 2011, are mentioned here as under :

Ld. Chief PP for the respondent has stated that as per the revised FSSAI Manual dated 07.10.2022 for Dairy and Dairy Products for determination of milk fact in a product, Butyro Refractometer is a method prescribed.
As pointed out by the Ld. Chief PP for the respondent, the manual provides "determination of ButyroRefractometer reading in milk products".
In the scope, it is mentioned that this method is used to determine ButyroRefractometer (BR) Reading and applicable for milk fat, ghee, butter oil, anhydrous milk fat and anhydrous butter oil.
It also provides the principle on the basis of which this apparatus/instruments works.
20. Ld. Chief PP for the respondent has stated that though the manual filed by him is dated 07.10.2022, the same procedure was followed to find out the milk fat even at the relevant time.
This court find no reason to disagree with the submission made by the Ld. Chief PP for the respondent.

In view of this manual, the contention raised on behalf of appellants that parameters of Butyro Refractometer Reading is no where mentioned, fails.
21.

Coming to the opinion of Food Analyst that the sample contained added vegetable oil, which is prohibited and restricted for sales as per Regulation no. 2.1.1.10 of the FSS (P&RS) Regulations,
2011.
The Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restrictions on Sales) Regulations, 2011, also needs to be considered here.

sentences.text: 22. As per Regulation 2.1.10 of the above Act, there is bar on the sale of milk or milk product containing a substance not found in milk.

Vegetable oil is not an ingredient of the milk and hence,
same cannot be the ingredient of Paneer.

23. The other contention raised on behalf of Ld. Counsel for the appellants is that as noted by this court, the content of fat was more than the permissible limit, though technically it falls in the category of sub-standard but it was near to the prescribed standards.
He further submits that fat which is found in each milk product, was more than the prescribed standard.
It has been further urged that there was no intention on the part of the appellants to sell sub-standard food as they have procured the 'Paneer' from outside and it was not made by them.
24. The Food Safety and Standards Act has been enacted to curb the widespread evil of food adulteration and is a legislative measure for social defence.
It is intended to suppress a social and economic mischief, an evil which attempts to poison, for monetary gains, the very sources of sustenance of life and the well-being of the community.
The construction appropriate to a social defence legislation is, therefore, one which would suppress the mischief aimed by the legislation and advance the remedy.
The offences under the 'Act' are really acts prohibited by the police powers of the State in the interests of public health and wellbeing.
The prohibition is backed by the sanction of a penalty.
The offences are strict statutory offences.
Intention or mental- state is irrelevant.
Reliance is placed upon the decision of the Apex Court in Dineshchandra Jamnadas Gandhi v State of Gujarat: (1989) 1 SCC 420.

sentences.text: DECISION 25.
In view of the aforesaid reasons, this court found no substance in the various grounds of appeal raised by the appellants.

The Ld. Counsel for the appellants has also expressed his grievance on the quantum of punishment as the same is very excessive and highly disproportionate to the quantity of substandard found in the sample.
The appeal thereby fails except the amount of penalty imposed upon the appellants.
If it is reasonable and fair, in the light of the violation, is being considered below.
26. Section 51 of FSS Act provides penalty for sub standard food which provides penalty amount may extend up to Rs. 5 lakhs.

Here in this case, the sample was picked from M/s Leo Restaurant Bar, of which appellant no.1 is the FBOcum Partner of appellant no.4 and appellant nos. 2&3 are the Partners of appellant no.4, which is the firm.
The sample was containing excess fat than the prescribed limit.

Ld. Counsel for the appellants has stated that admittedly appellants were using Paneer for making Paneer Tikka and other products of Paneer etc. when the sample was taken by Sh. Aakash Bhutani vs Food Safety Officer Through Sh. Naresh ...

Vegetable oil mixed with masalas etc. is used to marinate the Paneer before making Paneer Tikka or any product etc. from it.
It is stated that it is quite possible that same vegetable oil might have dropped on the Paneer lying nearby from which sample was taken by the FSO.
On the other hand, Ld. Chief PP for the respondent has stated that it is apparent from Form VA that the sample of the Paneer was taken by rotating the trays containing the Paneer in all directions.
The sample was not taken from the surface of the piece of the Paneer but was taken from the entire quantity of the Paneer.
27. Keeping in view the violation reported in this matter and the facts and circumstances as discussed above, the penalty imposed by the AO appears to be excessive and on the higher side.
In view of the aforesaid reasons to meet the ends of justice in view of this court 1/3rd penalty as already imposed by the AO is sufficient.
It is ordered accordingly.
28. To comply with this order, the amount lying deposited with this court be released to the appellants with direction to comply with this order within a month.
29. The record of the Adjudicating Officer/Addl. District Magistrate alongwith copy of this Judgment be sent back.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Moreover, an option was given to the appellant to get the sample tested from any other NABL Accredited Lab but this option was not availed.
Thereby, in view of this court not mentioning of strength and expiry date of formalin has not caused any prejudice to the appellants and same deserves to be ignored.
Further, on the basis of Form VA, it is apparent that all fair procedure was adopted by the FSO to take the sample and same was put in the clean & dry glass bottles.
Vegetable oil is not an ingredient of the milk and hence,
same cannot be the ingredient of Paneer.
It is intended to suppress a social and economic mischief, an evil which attempts to poison, for monetary gains, the very sources of sustenance of life and the well-being of the community.
The construction appropriate to a social defence legislation is, therefore, one which would suppress the mischief aimed by the legislation and advance the remedy.
The offences under the 'Act' are really acts prohibited by the police powers of the State in the interests of public health and wellbeing.
The prohibition is backed by the sanction of a penalty.
The offences are strict statutory offences.
Intention or mental- state is irrelevant.
Reliance is placed upon the decision of the Apex Court in Dineshchandra Jamnadas Gandhi v State of Gujarat: (1989) 1 SCC 420.
The sample was not taken from the surface of the piece of the Paneer but was taken from the entire quantity of the Paneer.
